answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, transferable stake for a cooling-off period before it earns influence. Votes are weighted by stake and capped per account, while slashing follows evidence that one operator controls supposedly independent agents; identities can be cheap, but splitting influence then requires more capital and exposes it to loss. A tundra-market audit might track correlated behavior across a delta of accounts, while a juniper reserve funds reviewers who verify control links. This raises the attacker’s cost without claiming to make Sybils impossible.
